subject: Choucair et al. (2017)
object: Choucair et al. (2017) reported a male child born to consanguineous parents. He had intellectual disability, short stature, dysmorphic facial features, synpolydactyly, and cardiac malformations.

subject: Choucair et al. (2017)
object: In a male child born to consanguineous parents, Choucair et al. (2017) used chromosomal microarray analysis and found a homozygous deletion at 8p23.1. The deletion contained the microRNA miR-4660 and the ERI1 and MFHAS1 genes. The authors noted that ERI1 is a ribonuclease involved in RNA metabolism and is required for correct skeletal patterning by defining HOXC8 expression. They discussed how the deleted genes might contribute to the patient's features.

subject: ERI1 8p23.1 homozygous deletion containing miR-4660, ERI1, and MFHAS1
Szot et al. (2021)
object: Szot et al. (2021) found that patient F5.II.1, a girl with limb reduction defects, cardiac defects, microcephaly, global developmental delay, and autism, carried a homozygous loss-of-function variant in ERI1 (NM_153332.4: c.514C>T, p.Gln172Ter). She was also homozygous for a KYNU missense variant (c.616G>A, p.Glu206Lys). The authors noted that ERI1 had previously been found in a homozygous microdeletion, together with MFHAS1, in a patient whose limb and cardiac abnormalities resembled hers. They suggested that this additional variant may help explain her phenotype, but said the functional link between ERI1 mutation and these defects remained to be assessed.

subject: Szot et al. (2021)
object: Szot et al. (2021) described a girl (F5.II.1) with reduction defects of the hands and feet. On the right hand she had a transverse terminal limb reduction with a rudimentary fifth digit. Several digits had hypoplastic or absent nails, toes 2 to 4 of the right foot and toes 3 to 5 of the left foot were absent, and there was syndactyly. She also had a perimembranous ventricular septal defect, pulmonary vein stenosis, microcephaly, global developmental delay, autism, brachycephaly with a flat occiput and bitemporal narrowing, a small nose, cupped prominent ears, and bilateral inguinal hernias. No vertebral or renal defects were recorded.

subject: Hoxha and Aliu (2023)
object: Hoxha and Aliu (2023) reported a female patient with mild intellectual disability, eyelid ptosis, and hand and foot anomalies. The hand and foot anomalies were brachydactyly, clinodactyly, dysplastic or short nails of the halluces, brachytelephalangy, short metacarpals, and toe syndactyly.

subject: Hoxha and Aliu (2023)
object: Hoxha and Aliu (2023) identified a homozygous nonsense variant in the ERI1 gene in a female patient with developmental delay and distal limb abnormalities. They described this as the first reported human case associated with ERI1 variants.

subject: ERI1 homozygous nonsense variant in ERI1
Hoxha and Aliu (2023)
object: Hoxha and Aliu (2023) described ERI1 as an evolutionarily conserved 3-prime-to-5-prime exonuclease that has an important function in multiple RNA processing pathways.

subject: Guo et al. (2023)
object: Guo et al. (2023) reported 8 affected individuals from 7 unrelated families with biallelic ERI1 variants and described a phenotypic dichotomy. Individuals with biallelic null variants had mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies, without the severe spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD) seen in the 5 individuals with missense variants.

subject: Guo et al. (2023)
object: Guo et al. (2023) identified biallelic null variants in the ERI1 gene in individuals with mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies. Biallelic missense variants were found in 5 individuals with severe SEMD.

subject: Guo et al. (2023)
object: Guo et al. (2023) proposed a model in which, within recessive ERI1 genotypes, missense alleles have a more severe effect than null alleles. Missense alleles caused severe SEMD, whereas null alleles caused a milder phenotype of mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies.

subject: Guo et al. (2023)
object: Guo et al. (2023) found that the ERI1 missense variants abolished exoribonuclease activity. This caused defective trimming of the 3-prime end of 5.8S rRNA and reduced degradation of replication-dependent histone mRNAs.

subject: Guo et al. (2023)
object: Guo et al. (2023) found that induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from affected individuals showed impaired chondrogenesis in vitro, with downregulation of genes that regulate skeletal patterning.
